name: Config Loader
description: Reads apprentice.yaml, parses YAML via pyyaml, validates all fields against Pydantic v2 models with strict mode. Handles env var references (env:VAR_NAME pattern) for API keys and secrets, resolving them at parse time via Pydantic BeforeValidator using validation context. Returns a fully typed, frozen/immutable ApprenticeConfig object. Fails at startup with clear, field-path-aware messages for missing required fields, invalid types, unknown evaluator types, unsupported backend combinations, missing env vars, and YAML syntax errors. No defaults for critical fields — everything must be explicit. Implemented as three cohesive units: models.py (Pydantic v2 schema), loader.py (pure loading function), errors.py (domain exceptions).

functions.name: load_config
functions.description: Main entry point: loads and validates an Apprentice configuration from a YAML file. Pure function with no internal state. Reads the file, parses YAML via yaml.safe_load(), resolves env:VAR_NAME references using the provided env mapping (or os.environ by default), constructs and validates ApprenticeConfig via Pydantic v2 with strict mode, and returns a frozen/immutable config object. All exceptions from the loading pipeline are caught and re-raised as domain-specific ConfigError subclasses with file path, field path, and clear messages.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Filesystem path to the apprentice.yaml configuration file.

inputs.name: env
inputs.description: String-to-string mapping for environment variable resolution. Defaults to os.environ at call time (not at definition time) for testability. Pass a dict in tests to avoid depending on real env vars.

functions.name: resolve_env_var
functions.description: Resolves an env:VAR_NAME reference string by looking up the variable name in the provided environment mapping. Used internally as a Pydantic BeforeValidator. If the input string does not start with 'env:', it is returned unchanged. If it does, the VAR_NAME portion is extracted and looked up in the env mapping. This function is exposed for testing but is primarily called within Pydantic's validation pipeline via validation context.

functions.name: validate_cross_field_constraints
functions.description: Performs all cross-field validations on a fully constructed ApprenticeConfig. Invoked as a @model_validator(mode='after') on ApprenticeConfig. Validates: threshold ordering (local_only >= local_ready), budget consistency (monthly >= daily), match fields exist in output schemas, evaluator-specific required fields are present, backend+field compatibility, and task name uniqueness. Returns the config if valid, raises ConfigValidationError with all collected violations if not.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: The fully constructed ApprenticeConfig to validate cross-field constraints on.

error_cases.condition: One or more cross-field constraints are violated

error_data.message: Cross-field validation failed with {count} error(s)

preconditions: All individual field validations have already passed (this runs in mode='after')
config is a fully constructed ApprenticeConfig instance
postconditions: For every evaluator in every task: all match_field names exist in that task's output_schema
Every semantic_similarity evaluator has a non-empty semantic_model
Every llm_judge evaluator has a non-empty judge_prompt_template
Every regex_match evaluator has a non-empty regex_pattern
Every json_schema_match evaluator has a non-empty json_schema_path
All task_name values are unique across the tasks list
Remote finetuning backends (openai, anyscale) have api_key and api_base_url set
The returned config is the same object, unmodified (frozen model)

invariants: ApprenticeConfig is frozen/immutable after construction — no mutation is possible
All SecretStr fields mask their values in repr and str — secrets never appear in logs or error messages
All env:VAR_NAME references are resolved at parse time — no deferred resolution at runtime
Config validation is exhaustive — if load_config returns without error, the config is fully valid for all downstream components
No silent defaults for critical fields — api keys, model names, task definitions, budget limits, and backend selection must always be explicitly specified
Extra/unknown fields in YAML always cause validation failure (extra='forbid') — no silent field dropping
Strict type coercion — '3' as a string is not accepted where int is expected (strict=True)
All task_name values in the config are unique
Cross-field constraints are enforced atomically — either all pass or the entire config is rejected
The loader function is pure and stateless — calling it twice with the same inputs produces identical results
YAML parsing uses safe_load only — no arbitrary Python object deserialization
